# ciphertrust_azure_certificate (Resource)

Use this resource to add a certificate to a CipherTrust Manager Azure vault. The mode is chosen by which block is set. Only one block can be set.

- No block (default): creates a new certificate in the vault from azure_params.
- upload_certificate: imports an existing certificate and private key.
- restore_certificate: restores a purged certificate from the backup of the latest version retained in CipherTrust Manager, into the vault nominated by vault_id.

All inputs are immutable except `azure_params.tags` and `azure_params.policy.attributes.enabled`, which are updated in place.

To create a new version of a certificate, create another certificate resource with the same name.

If a soft-deleted certificate of the same name exists in the vault, creating the resource recovers it instead of creating a new certificate. Importing a soft-deleted certificate also recovers it. Both require `recover_soft_deleted_certificates` to be true in the provider settings, otherwise they fail.

On destroy, the certificate is soft-deleted and, if purge_certificates_on_delete is true in the provider settings (the default) and the vault supports purge, purged. If it is false, the certificate is only soft-deleted.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Pre-requisites for an Azure certificate - Azure connection, Azure vault.
# This file shows the available options and need not be valid as a whole.

# Provider settings that affect Azure certificates. All are optional.
provider "ciphertrust" {
  cloud_key_manager = {
    azure = {
      # On destroy, purge a certificate after it is soft-deleted, if purge is
      # supported by the vault. Default is true. If false, the certificate is
      # only soft-deleted.
      purge_certificates_on_delete = true

      # If creating a certificate fails because the name belongs to a soft-deleted
      # certificate, recover that certificate instead. Default is false.
      recover_soft_deleted_certificates = false
    }
  }
}

# Native certificate created in the vault.
resource "ciphertrust_azure_certificate" "native" {
  name     = "native-certificate"
  vault_id = ciphertrust_azure_vault.vault.id
  azure_params = {
    policy = {
      issuer = {
        name = "Self"
      }
      key_props = {
        kty        = "RSA"
        key_size   = 2048
        exportable = true
        reuse_key  = false
      }
      x509_props = {
        subject         = "CN=example.com"
        validity_months = 12
        sans = {
          dns_names = ["example.com"]
        }
      }
      lifetime_actions = [
        {
          trigger = {
            days_before_expiry = 30
          }
          action = {
            action_type = "AutoRenew"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
    tags = {
      environment = "test"
    }
  }
}

# Certificate signed by a CipherTrust Manager CA, uploaded to the vault.
# ca_id, source_cert_id and private_key_pem are all required.
# With upload_certificate only azure_params.tags can be set. policy cannot be set.
resource "ciphertrust_azure_certificate" "cm_signed" {
  name     = "cm-signed-certificate"
  vault_id = ciphertrust_azure_vault.vault.id
  azure_params = {
    tags = {
      environment = "dev"
    }
  }
  upload_certificate = {
    source_cert_id  = "cipher-trust-certificate-id"
    ca_id           = "cipher-trust-ca-id"
    private_key_pem = "/path/to/private-key.pem"
  }
}

# External PEM certificate using file paths.
# A PEM certificate needs private_key_pem.
resource "ciphertrust_azure_certificate" "external_pem_files" {
  name     = "external-pem-files"
  vault_id = ciphertrust_azure_vault.vault.id
  upload_certificate = {
    certificate     = "/path/to/certificate.pem"
    private_key_pem = "/path/to/private-key.pem"
  }
}

# External PEM certificate using PEM content from variables.
resource "ciphertrust_azure_certificate" "external_pem_content" {
  name     = "external-pem-content"
  vault_id = ciphertrust_azure_vault.vault.id
  upload_certificate = {
    certificate     = var.certificate_pem
    private_key_pem = var.private_key_pem
  }
}

# External PFX file using a file path.
# A PFX contains the private key, so private_key_pem is not set.
# private_key_password is only needed if the PFX is password protected. It is also used
# for an encrypted private_key_pem.
resource "ciphertrust_azure_certificate" "external_pfx_file" {
  name     = "external-pfx-file"
  vault_id = ciphertrust_azure_vault.vault.id
  upload_certificate = {
    certificate          = "/path/to/certificate.pfx"
    private_key_password = var.private_key_password
  }
}

# External PFX supplied as base64 text, for example from filebase64().
# private_key_password is only needed if the PFX is password protected.
resource "ciphertrust_azure_certificate" "external_pfx_base64" {
  name     = "external-pfx-base64"
  vault_id = ciphertrust_azure_vault.vault.id
  upload_certificate = {
    certificate          = filebase64("/path/to/certificate.pfx")
    private_key_password = var.private_key_password
  }
}

# Restore a purged certificate into a vault from its CipherTrust Manager backup.
# name and azure_params cannot be set.
resource "ciphertrust_azure_certificate" "restored" {
  vault_id = ciphertrust_azure_vault.vault.id
  restore_certificate = {
    certificate_id = "purged-certificate-id"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `vault_id` (String) (Conditionally immutable) CipherTrust Manager resource ID of the Azure vault that contains the certificate. Can only be changed if the previously configured vault no longer exists in CipherTrust Manager. When restore_certificate is set this is the vault the certificate is restored to; it can be any vault. A vault name is not accepted.

### Optional

- `azure_params` (Attributes) Azure certificate parameters. Only `tags` and `policy.attributes.enabled` can be updated, everything else is immutable. `policy` is required unless `upload_certificate` is set. When `upload_certificate` is set only `tags` can be set. Cannot be set when `restore_certificate` is set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params))
- `name` (String) (Immutable) Name of the certificate. May contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Required unless restore_certificate is set, in which case it cannot be set.
- `restore_certificate` (Attributes) (Immutable) Restores a purged certificate into `vault_id` instead of creating a new one. Cannot be combined with `name`, `azure_params` or `upload_certificate`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--restore_certificate))
- `upload_certificate` (Attributes) (Immutable) Uploads a certificate to the vault instead of creating a new one. There are two ways to upload. Either set `source_cert_id`, `ca_id` and `private_key_pem` to upload a certificate signed by a CipherTrust Manager CA, or set `certificate` to upload an external certificate (a PEM certificate with `private_key_pem`, or a PFX). `certificate` cannot be combined with `source_cert_id` or `ca_id`. Only `azure_params.tags` can be set with it. Cannot be combined with `azure_params.policy` or `restore_certificate`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--upload_certificate))

### Read-Only

- `azure_created_at` (String) Time the certificate was created in Azure.
- `azure_expire_at` (String) Time the certificate expires.
- `azure_updated_at` (String) Time the certificate was last updated in Azure.
- `backup` (String) Backup of the certificate.
- `backup_at` (String) Time the certificate was last backed up.
- `cert` (String) Base64 encoded certificate (CER).
- `cert_material_origin` (String) Origin of the certificate material.
- `cert_soft_deleted_in_azure` (Boolean) Whether the certificate is soft-deleted in Azure.
- `cert_source` (String) Source of the certificate.
- `cid` (String) Azure identifier of the certificate.
- `cloud_name` (String) Azure cloud of the vault.
- `created_at` (String) Time the certificate was created in CipherTrust Manager.
- `deleted` (Boolean) Whether the certificate is deleted.
- `error` (String) Error reported for the certificate.
- `gone` (Boolean) Whether the certificate no longer exists in Azure.
- `id` (String) CipherTrust Manager resource ID of the certificate.
- `key_vault` (String) Name of the Azure vault that contains the certificate.
- `kid` (String) Azure identifier of the key backing the certificate.
- `operation` (String) Last operation performed on the certificate.
- `operation_error` (String) Error of the last operation, if it failed.
- `recoverable_days` (Number) Number of days a soft-deleted certificate can be recovered.
- `recovery_level` (String) Azure recovery level of the certificate.
- `region` (String) Azure region of the vault.
- `rotated_at` (String) Time the certificate was last rotated.
- `sid` (String) Azure identifier of the secret backing the certificate.
- `soft_delete_enabled` (Boolean) Whether soft delete is enabled on the vault.
- `status` (String) Status of the certificate.
- `synced_at` (String) Time the certificate was last synchronized with Azure.
- `tenant` (String) Azure tenant of the vault.
- `thumbprint` (String) Thumbprint of the certificate.
- `updated_at` (String) Time the certificate was last updated in CipherTrust Manager.
- `version` (String) Azure version of the certificate.
- `version_count` (Number) Number of versions of the certificate.

<a id="nestedatt--azure_params"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params`

Optional:

- `policy` (Attributes) Certificate policy. Only `attributes.enabled` can be updated, everything else is immutable. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy))
- `tags` (Map of String) Application specific metadata in the form of key-value pairs. Can be updated. An update replaces the whole set of tags. Removing the attribute from the configuration does not clear the tags, set it to an empty map (`tags = {}`) to remove all tags.

<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy`

Optional:

- `attributes` (Attributes) Attributes of the certificate. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--attributes))
- `issuer` (Attributes) Issuer of the certificate. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--issuer))
- `key_props` (Attributes) Properties of the key backing the certificate. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--key_props))
- `lifetime_actions` (Attributes List) (Immutable) Actions to perform on the certificate during its lifetime. Only one action is allowed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--lifetime_actions))
- `secret_props` (Attributes) Properties of the secret backing the certificate. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--secret_props))
- `x509_props` (Attributes) X509 properties of the certificate. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--x509_props))

<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--attributes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.attributes`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the certificate is enabled. Can be updated.

Read-Only:

- `activation_date` (String) Date of certificate activation in UTC time in RFC3339 format. Derived by Azure and cannot be set.
- `expiration_date` (String) Date of certificate expiry in UTC time in RFC3339 format. Derived by Azure from x509_props.validity_months and cannot be set.


<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--issuer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.issuer`

Required:

- `name` (String) (Immutable) Name of the issuer. Set to Self for a self-signed certificate.

Optional:

- `cert_transparency` (Boolean) (Immutable) Whether the certificate is published to certificate transparency logs. Not valid for the Self issuer.
- `certificate_type` (String) (Immutable) Optional certificate type that is specific to the issuer, for example OV-SSL or EV-SSL. Not used by the Self issuer.


<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--key_props"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.key_props`

Required:

- `kty` (String) (Immutable) Key type. Options are EC, EC-HSM, RSA and RSA-HSM.

Optional:

- `curve` (String) (Immutable) Elliptic curve name. Options are P-256, P-384, P-521 and SECP256K1.
- `exportable` (Boolean) (Immutable) Whether the private key can be exported. Not valid for HSM keys.
- `key_size` (Number) (Immutable) Size of an RSA key. Options are 2048, 3072 and 4096.
- `reuse_key` (Boolean) (Immutable) Whether the same key pair is used when the certificate is renewed.


<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--lifetime_actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.lifetime_actions`

Optional:

- `action` (Attributes) Action to perform. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--lifetime_actions--action))
- `trigger` (Attributes) Condition that runs the action. Set either lifetime_percentage or days_before_expiry. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--lifetime_actions--trigger))

<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--lifetime_actions--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.lifetime_actions.action`

Required:

- `action_type` (String) (Immutable) Type of the action. Options are AutoRenew and EmailContacts.


<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--lifetime_actions--trigger"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.lifetime_actions.trigger`

Optional:

- `days_before_expiry` (Number) (Immutable) Number of days before expiry at which the action runs.
- `lifetime_percentage` (Number) (Immutable) Percentage of the lifetime at which the action runs. Between 1 and 99.



<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--secret_props"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.secret_props`

Optional:

- `content_type` (String) (Immutable) Content type of the certificate. For example application/x-pkcs12 or application/x-pem-file.


<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--x509_props"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.x509_props`

Required:

- `subject` (String) (Immutable) Subject name. Must be a valid X509 distinguished name.

Optional:

- `enhanced_key_usage` (List of String) (Immutable) Enhanced key usage object identifiers.
- `key_usage` (List of String) (Immutable) Allowed key usages. For example digitalSignature or keyEncipherment.
- `sans` (Attributes) Subject alternative names. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_params--policy--x509_props--sans))
- `validity_months` (Number) (Immutable) Number of months the certificate is valid for.

<a id="nestedatt--azure_params--policy--x509_props--sans"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_params.policy.x509_props.sans`

Optional:

- `dns_names` (List of String) (Immutable) Domain names.
- `emails` (List of String) (Immutable) Email addresses.
- `user_principal_names` (List of String) (Immutable) User principal names.





<a id="nestedatt--restore_certificate"></a>
### Nested Schema for `restore_certificate`

Required:

- `certificate_id` (String) CipherTrust Manager resource ID of the purged certificate to restore. It is no longer in Terraform state.


<a id="nestedatt--upload_certificate"></a>
### Nested Schema for `upload_certificate`

Optional:

- `ca_id` (String) (Immutable) CipherTrust Manager resource ID of the CA that signed the certificate. Requires source_cert_id. Cannot be used with certificate.
- `certificate` (String, Sensitive) (Immutable) External certificate to upload. Cannot be used with source_cert_id or ca_id. Can be PEM content, the path to a PEM or PFX file, or a base64 encoded PFX. Requires private_key_pem when it is a PEM certificate. A path is read by the provider, relative to the directory Terraform runs from. A PFX file is base64 encoded by the provider. A base64 encoded PFX is sent as is.
- `private_key_password` (String, Sensitive) (Immutable) Password used to decrypt private_key_pem or the PFX in certificate, if it is encrypted.
- `private_key_pem` (String, Sensitive) (Immutable) Private key of the certificate, as PEM content or the path to a PEM file. Required with source_cert_id and ca_id, or with a PEM certificate. Not used with a PFX. A path is read by the provider, relative to the directory Terraform runs from.
- `source_cert_id` (String) (Immutable) CipherTrust Manager resource ID of the certificate to upload. Requires ca_id and private_key_pem. Cannot be used with certificate. The value is kept as configured. It is not read back from CipherTrust Manager.
